kicker: Shipbuilding · naval programmes still in tender
title: Up to ₹1.5 lakh cr of naval ships is still in tender
dek: Frigates, mine-countermeasure vessels and landing docks worth up to ₹1.4 lakh cr are out for bids or due this year, about 4x the order books of Cochin Shipyard and GRSE combined. Only Cochin's ₹5,000 cr survey-vessel deal is close.

Ships for Indian owners in 10 years

read: The yards' next decade sits in tenders, not contracts; Cochin's survey-vessel signing is the first test, and the three big programmes have no award dates.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q1 FY27 earnings calls of Cochin Shipyard and GRSE and Q2 FY27 call of Bharat Electronics; Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
notes: Values are indicative programme sizes cited by management on Q1 FY27 calls (August 2026), the latest shipyard calls on the desk, not contract values. The yards differ on P-17 Bravo (Cochin about ₹49,000 cr; GRSE cites the ₹70,000 cr Defence Acquisition Council approval) and on landing docks (₹32,000–35,000 cr); bars use the upper end, so the total is ₹1.25–1.5 lakh cr. GRSE lists P-17 Bravo and the 120 interceptor craft among about ₹80,000 cr of live bids, and expects the mine-countermeasure and landing-dock tenders in calendar 2026; Cochin gave no award timeline for the three large programmes. Cochin is lowest bidder for five survey vessels (about ₹5,000 cr), with signing guided around November 2026. Order books are as of June 2026; the Next Generation Corvette contracts for GRSE and GSL were signed, according to Bharat Electronics' Q2 call, and are not shown.
